If one imagines that the masses of flames arising from his hand-symbols burn and reduce to ashes the host of obstacles dwelling in the ten directions, it is shown that at that time "the wind and so forth will be pacified." The phrase "if such a nature is not realized" and so forth indicates that without such meditation, the activity of the Yogini, which consists of drawing the mandala, will not be accomplished. Here too, in wrathful activities, the "killing of the seed" by the syllable **Phaṭ**, which kills the obstacles of both one's own school and other schools, should be applied at the time when enemies cause harm. Now, concerning the phrase "now" and so forth: a yogi who practices with elaboration dwells in a three-storied divine palace. Having directed the mind toward the Wisdom Body <term>jñānakāya</term> of whichever deity one identifies with—such as **Vairocana** through self-consecration—and having placed the four seals <term>mudrā</term> of the commitment <term>samaya</term>, who are beautiful in form and very well adorned, in the four directions, one then enjoys the five sensory qualities together with them. It is shown that by the stages of meditative union, withdrawal <term>pratyāhāra</term>, and meditative concentration <term>dhyāna</term>, one will experience Great Bliss <term>mahāsukha</term>. "Generated through the stage of wisdom" refers to the elaboration through the stage of self-consecration. The phrase "that application" is a brief presentation. "Visualizing in an instant" is the detailed explanation. By that, the stages such as "obtaining the proximity of appearance" are refuted. "In the center of the four seats" means in the center of the seats of the four goddesses. The phrase "the body of the Great Vajradhara" is merely an illustration; one should also meditate on the bodies of **Vairocana** and the others. "By knowing the reality of the deity" means knowing the four goddesses together with oneself as the essence of the five wisdoms. "In the places of **Locanā** and the others" refers to the East and other directions. Through that stage of total purity, the obsession with external objects is abandoned, and acting like an ordinary person is also refuted
head: Whenever these occur, at that time, from the complete transformation of the Lord **Amitābha**, one imagines oneself as the noble **Hayagrīva**, with three faces, six arms, and three eyes, standing in the posture with the left leg extended

—oneself as the Noble <term>Hayagriva</term> <gloss>Horse-Necked One</gloss>, having three faces, six arms, three eyes, and standing in the <term>alidha</term> <gloss>left leg extended</gloss> posture. If one imagines the mass of flames arising from his hand-implements burning the hosts of obstacles dwelling in the ten directions and turning them to ash, then at that time "wind and the others will be pacified." 

By the phrase "if such a nature is not realized," it means that if one does not meditate on this, the activity of the <term>Yogini</term> who is the essence of drawing the mandala will not be accomplished. Here too, in fierce activities, the "killing of the seed" with the syllable <term>PHAT</term>, which kills the obstacles of one's own or others' schools, "should be applied at the time when the enemy is causing harm."

Regarding the phrase "now," and so forth: a practitioner of the "elaborate" <note>the path involving external ritual and complex visualization</note> type dwells in a three-tiered divine palace. Having blessed oneself, one focuses on the <term>jnanasattva</term> <gloss>wisdom-being</gloss> body of <term>Vairocana</term> or any other deity. <insert>Place the four symbolic seals</insert> who are of beautiful form and very well-adorned in the four directions. It is shown that by "experiencing the five sensory qualities" together with them, entering into union, and following the stages of "withdrawal" and "meditative concentration," one will "experience Great Bliss." 

"Arising through the stages of wisdom" refers to the elaborate sequence of blessing oneself. The phrase "its application" is a brief teaching. "Focusing in an instant" is the detailed explanation. Therefore, the sequence of "attaining appearance" and so forth is refuted <note>suggesting a sudden rather than gradual realization in this specific context</note>. 

"In the center of the four seats" means in the center of the seats of the four goddesses.
